notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($45,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Colorado county candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Colorado yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Pueblo County Sheriff's Office operates eight drones as of 2018, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS003738, citing Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2023 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included. Residents also pay Pueblo County.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Colorado city candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 90 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Pueblo's borders in OpenStreetMap (23 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Colorado yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 23 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Pueblo's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.

source.label: OpenStreetMap license-plate cameras (as mapped by DeFlock)

redFlags.label: Real-time crime center
redFlags.detail: The Pueblo Police Department launched a real-time crime center in 2024.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS013976, citing KOAA

redFlags.label: Gunshot detection (ShotSpotter)
redFlags.detail: The Pueblo Police Department installed Shotspotter over three square miles in 2023.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS013277, citing SoundThinking

redFlags.label: Third-party investigative platform
redFlags.detail: The Pueblo Police Department received an enterprise license for LexisNexis' Accurint Virtual Crime Center through its membership in the Colorado Information Sharing Consortium.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS012777, citing Government information

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: The Pueblo Police Department began using ELSAG automated license plate readers in 2010. PPD added another ALPR system in 2018. The Pueblo Transportation Department also added Nupark ALPR systems, which is checked against the Pueblo Police Department's hot lists.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS000044, citing City of Pueblo Colorado

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Pueblo Police Department operates two DJI drones as of 2018, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS003739, citing Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College
